TensorStudio / 02
02 / THE PRODUCT JOURNEY

From “what is Bittensor?”
to “show me the result.”

01 · Learn with Quest

Explore a pixel world, answer quizzes and practise concepts in local code exercises.

02 · Build in Studio

Clarify the task, generate editable code and interact with a browser preview.

03 · Observe with TensorScan

Inspect real blocks, decoded calls, events, accounts and subnet participants.

04 · Plan operations

Explore compute drafts, recorded events and billing in the separate TensorNode workspace.

Task → Labelled examples → Recipe → Offline scoring → Miner logs → Signed request → Chain observations

Quest and TensorNode are separate companion apps. Studio connects the learning journey; no shared backend integration is implied.

Why Bittensor?

A subnet defines a task. Miners produce work. Validators evaluate it. The network coordinates incentives.

Studio helps builders make that task and evaluation concrete, then inspect their development experiment alongside real chain data.

Bittensor network concepts ↗

Public exploration and bounded AI are available without sign-in. Process execution remains owner-protected. Development inference is distinct from registered subnet participation.

ACTUAL CAPTURE · SIGNED MINER REQUEST + RESPONSE
“As soon as I log in,
the screen freezes.”
MODEL CLASSIFICATIONtechnicalHTTP 200 · signed development request
  • Editable support-inbox prototype with manual review.
  • Labelled examples and reviewed project assembly.
  • Offline fixture scoring, process logs and console output.
  • Independent public testnet observations in TensorScan.

Offline scores use fixture responses and simulated timing. The miner response is real inference. No on-chain registration, reward earnings or paid GPU execution is claimed.
